submission.natural_language_explanation:
Local newline-clustering head: it peaks (0.7-1.0 of max) on a bare '
' token (id 187) when one or more other '
' tokens sit within the previous ~4 tokens, i.e. the second newline of a blank line or a line break that ends a short one- or two-token line (headings, 'A:', menu items, list rows), and it attends back to those earlier newlines. A lone '
' ending a long line, merged whitespace tokens at the end of text, and ordinary words and punctuation stay at a baseline of about 0.2-0.45 of max.
